title: SIPP care constraints diverge by income-to-poverty band
source_unit: SIPP person record by reference month, stratified by monthly household income-to-poverty ratio, using final person and Fay-BRR replicate weights

denominator.unit: positive-final-person-weight selected person-record/month rows; each measure has its own valid universe

observations.method: Official child-care status flags and conditional universes; WPFINWGT full estimate and 240 Fay-BRR replicate weights with G=240 and perturbation factor 0.5.
observations.uncertainty: Intervals are design-based approximations; the time-lost cell is small and imprecise. Income-to-poverty bands are monthly household context repeated on person records.
observations.subgroup: Monthly household income-to-poverty ratio below 1.00x; payment/assistance, work-prevention, and time-lost measures retain distinct universes.
observations.counterinterpretation: The lower-income band has higher work-prevention and assistance shares than the upper bands, but this is descriptive and does not identify eligibility, need, provider supply, or causal effects.

denominator.unit: positive-final-person-weight selected person-record/month rows; each measure has its own valid universe

observations.method: Same official-universe and Fay-BRR method as the other income bands.
observations.uncertainty: Intervals are design-based approximations; the time-lost cell is small and highly imprecise.
observations.counterinterpretation: Assistance and work prevention can coexist; the estimate does not show whether assistance arrived before or after a work constraint.

denominator.unit: positive-final-person-weight selected person-record/month rows; each measure has its own valid universe

observations.method: Same official-universe and Fay-BRR method as the other income bands.
observations.uncertainty: Intervals are design-based approximations; time lost remains conditional and less precise than the broader care measures.
observations.counterinterpretation: A lower payment-assistance share may reflect different eligibility, arrangements, reporting, or resources; it does not measure unmet need.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; 4.00x poverty threshold or more

denominator.unit: positive-final-person-weight selected person-record/month rows; each measure has its own valid universe

observations.method: Same official-universe and Fay-BRR method as the other income bands.
observations.uncertainty: Intervals are design-based approximations; time lost remains a small conditional cell.
observations.subgroup: Monthly household income-to-poverty ratio 4.00x or more.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher paid-care use in this band does not mean lower-income families have less care need; arrangements, resources, work, and eligibility differ.

related_sources.claim: Official field labels, status flags, universes, and income-to-poverty definitions.

boundary: This is a person-weighted, design-based subgroup comparison. It does not establish household prevalence, causal care effects, eligibility, provider access, time substitution, recovery, trust, or political action.
